vedic_reference.note: Goddess Karpagam is a form of Goddess Saraswati, the goddess of knowledge and learning. She is also known as Vidyavalli (knowledge giver) and Vidya (knowledge). The name Karpagavalli signifies a wish-fulfilling tree of knowledge and learning.

data.cultural_impact: The name Karpagavalli holds significant cultural importance in Hindu traditions, representing a symbol of abundance, prosperity, and fulfillment. It is often used as a name for girls, reflecting the deep reverence and respect for the divine power embodied by the Goddess Karpagam.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, Karpagavalli is considered a manifestation of the divine mother, who nurtures and cares for her children. The name represents the deep love and compassion of the divine, as well as the hope and faith that one can have in the power of the universe to grant their deepest desires and aspirations.

historical_references.reference: Karpagavalli was a revered woman saint of the 12th century in the Hindu tradition, venerated particularly in the Tamil region of South India. She is considered to be an incarnation of the goddess Mariamman, and is believed to have performed numerous miracles during her lifetime.

Another reference states that Karpagavalli was a devotee of Lord Subramanya who lived in the 7th century in the region of Tirunelveli, Tamil Nadu. She is known for her intense devotion and self-sacrifice, and is believed to have attained divine union with the deity.
